text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Medical workers in Eastern Slavonia sign up for employment by the government health authories.
- Reshuffle at Rijeka's port company: Ante Dropulic appointed as new director.
- Residents of Osijek fear floods as level of the Drava river rises to 405 cm. Emergency measures to be enforced if it reaches 470 cm.
- Organisers of the soccer match between Croatia and Partizan prepared for Wednesday: The match also to be broadcast on a large video screen outside the Maksimir stadium.
- State guarantee agency launches a new programme of credit support for small enterprises. Individual loans of up to 360,000 kuna to be granted to private entreprenuers.
- Shareholders of Osijek's brewery give a green light for a 70 million kuna takeover by Brodokomerc company.
- Pensions to rise 3.3 percent in August to make up for an increase in living costs. Some 150,000 pensioners who now receive a 100-kuna supplement to their monthly income not to get a raise.
- Oil firm INA and Korea's Samsung sign an agreement for expanding cooperation and say they will consider joint exploration projects in the future.

- Porec's hotelier Riviera records one millionth overnight stay several days earlier than last year and plans to reach the figure of two million overnights in September. The company sees this year's pre-tax profit at 15 million kuna on income of 235 million.
- Blitzkrieg in empty docks: Crisis in the ailing Rijeka port culminates with sacking of the old company management and appointment of a new board.

- Commentary: Croatian diplomacy will have a busy summer countering the mounting pressure from the international community. An urgent goal is to draw the country out of isolation. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
